comments.author: hatthew
comments.text:
This analogy doesn't hold at all. Casinos are engineered for the house to win and the customer to lose because the casino is paying the customer directly. They are disincentivized to let the customer win. If the customer always won, the casino goes out of business very quickly.
Ad auctions are completely different, since they are just a marketplace. A customer's (advertiser's) win comes from a third party, and the point of the ad platform is to connect that third party to the customer. The ad platform would
love
to be able to make every single customer win all the time. Although, if they did that, it would create a lot more demand and even out the ROI with increased ad prices. But that's not the "evil ad platform" engineering the customers to always lose in the way casinos do, that's simply basic supply/demand economics.

comments.author: natch
comments.text:
Apple has significantly weakened its security assurances in a way that is arguably deceptive. They used to say nobody can access your data, not even Apple. Now they say Apple cannot access your data. People will point out that your key is created on your device, lives on your device, and never leaves your device, but that is just your key. Your key is likely a KEK (key encryption key) that opens another key (not “your” key, let’s call it the actual key) that your data is secured with. There can be other parties (UK government) with their own KEK that opens a copy of the actual key. In this scenario, Apple can have no access to a KEK that opens the actual key, but they are forced to make the wording change they did, if they want to stay honest.
I say the statement is arguably deceptive because it presents the same feel of assurance that the old one did, to most people.
Note John Ternus in a recent event (WWDC keynote if I recall correctly) used the old wording. I think this was a slip-up (I’d hate to think it was a calculated lie posing as a slip-up).

stories.title_en: Fuck Your AI Safeguards

comments.author: SkyeCA
comments.text:
The safeguards are the future of closed AI and the increasing number of tasks Claude refuses to help with has been a big wake-up call to me.
The closed models can only get more restricted as time goes on and they're going to be a dead end if you want to do anything outside the norm. Claude
already
refuses to do things that it was fine assisting me with a month ago.
I completely refuse to accept a computer telling me I'm not allowed to do something, so I've been increasingly using open, self-hosted models.

comments.author: espeed
comments.text:
No one should use Fable 5.2 going forward. Anthropic officially added silent degradation back, "Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 perform at about the level of Opus 5.5":
"Thus, in relevant areas, including accelerator kernel optimization and improving large language model architectures, Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 perform at about the level of Opus 5.5...Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 also include transparent fallbacks to Opus 5 for a small set of topics in this domain, including kernel development on certain nonstandard accelerators."
https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2#safety...
How do you know when you trip a safeguard and are getting a degraded model? You never know when it is going to degrade. Having to wonder if the model is degraded and is trashing your code is how you destroy user trust. If this practice remains for future models, no one should use Anthropic going forward.

comments.author: nathanfig
comments.text:
This had real consequences during the HuggingFace attack- closed models refused to help, GLM-5 is what HuggingFace used to thwart the swarm.
More importantly, it showcases how little teeth the Claude constitution has. Claude will reassure users that its constitution means it prioritizes user autonomy and privacy, but will quickly admit how meaningless that is when "safeguards" override Claude.
That is to say, the constitutional approach to Claude seems weak and even misleading if said constitution puts no constraint on Anthropic.
